limitations: The unstable pocket of D2Q9 BGK inside this window is localised at wave vectors that a 32x32 box cannot represent; the box-grid prediction and the measurement agree with each other (<=1%) while sitting slightly below the fine-grid boundary (<=1.5%).

D2Q9 has an exactly neutral (|mu| = 1) checkerboard branch at (pi, 0) and (0, pi) for every tau; it carries no momentum, so a velocity-residual measurement cannot see it and reports faster decay than the marginal prediction there.
Measured growth is fitted over the linear window only; amplification factors above 1.3 saturate within a few steps and their fits carry several-percent error.
The oracle tiers are upper envelopes over a declared discrete rate set, not proofs of optimality.

m1_exchange_law.criterion: absolute amplification-factor deviation <= 5e-3 for |sigma_pred| >= 0.005; relative growth-rate deviation <= 5% for |sigma_pred| >= 0.03; near-marginal points (|sigma_pred| < 0.005) are reported but excluded, because the neutral checkerboard branch at (pi, 0)/(0, pi) carries no momentum and is invisible to a velocity-residual measurement

m3_negative_controls.broadband_detector_note: the literal 10-step ratio > 1e3 detector fires only for lambda > 1e3**(1/10) = 1.995, so it is a deep-instability detector; the marginal verdict uses the fitted growth rate

specificity_probe.note: A non-orthogonal basis alone (all rates inside (0, 2)) is neutral at 2/3 probe points but does destabilise at 1 of them (the low-tau corner, where the same kinetic pocket is already active).  So the basis defect is *not* silently ignored; it simply requires the pocket to exist.  The must-fail control set combines the basis defect with an out-of-range rate, where both routes fire unambiguously.
